subject: SDK shim + short-term runtime workaround for BrightLane POC
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK shim + short-term runtime workaround for BrightLane POC

Team —

BrightLane (contact: Alex Zhou) hit us with two progressive issues during their mobile POC this morning. Summary:

1) Their iOS client is on an older networking stack and fails if we do strict chunked transfer / streaming semantics without an HTTP/1.1 compatibility shim in the SDK. They asked for a light-weight "shim" that toggles a compatibility header and falls back to short payloads rather than full streaming frames.

2) They also reported inconsistent embeddings when using small streaming sequences with prefix caching enabled. In their logs we see a mismatch between the generated tokens and the cached KV state (small seqs + rapid reconnects). They want a short-term mitigation (runtime toggle) to disable prefix/KV caching for sequences under ~64 tokens while we root-cause.

Attachments: brightlane-interop-notes.pdf (field logs + minimal repro)
HubSpot: HBP-9421

Asks / constraints:
- BrightLane is on a soft timebox: they want a workable mitigation within 10 business days to keep the POC going.
- Any runtime change must be narrowly scoped and reversible — they prefer a config flag per-customer / per-deployment rather than a default change.

Can platform/runtime and SDK triage this and propose an implementation timeline? Marissa — can you forward the exact sequence of steps from their mobile team (logs attached)? Dev — would a temporary runtime flag be safe to gate to dedicated customers only? Karthik — we may need product prioritization / security review.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK shim + short-term runtime workaround for BrightLane POC

Thanks Evelyn — I reviewed the attached notes briefly. A couple quick points from infra/runtime:

- Disabling KV/prefix caching for very short sequences is straightforward as a runtime flag; we can gate it by customer id or by deployment (Dedicated/Private). Risk is low if it remains off by default.
- The mismatch you describe could come from: (a) application-level reconnection with stale client-side context, (b) an edge-level retransmit that causes duplicate partial KV updates, or (c) an SDK that replays requests without the same cache keys. The logs will help narrow it down.

Questions:
1) Can Marissa pull a minimal repro that includes the exact HTTP request/response frames and sequence IDs? (We need to see the connect/disconnect/replay pattern.)
2) Are we sure BrightLane is on Dedicated or Hosted? Per-customer flagging differs by mode.

If we get a repro today I can prototype a toggle: runtime config "disable_kvcache_for_short_seq=true" and an SDK header "X-Redwood-Compat: shim-v1". That will be our proposed short-term mitigation.

I'll mock an RFC and estimate dev + QA: approx 3 dev-days + 1 qa-day for a narrow toggle, plus an operations roll (can be canaried).

- Dev
Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLane mobile repro + logs

Forwarding the mobile team's note and the minimal repro they attached. Repro steps are small — they initiate a streaming generation, drop connectivity after ~30 tokens, and re-open a new connection that resumes with an assumption of prior state.

---- Forwarded message ----
From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@brightlane.ai>
To: poc@brightlane.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: POC - streaming mismatch on iOS client

Marissa,

We hit this while demoing to our data team. Steps to reproduce:
1) Open session via mobile app (mobile-sdk v0.9.8).
2) Start streaming generation (prompt ~20 tokens).
3) Simulate flaky network (toggle airplane mode) -> app reconnects and issues a resume request.
4) New response contains tokens inconsistent with earlier output; sometimes final embedding vector also shifts.

Attached: ios-nettrace.log, replay-frames.json

We need a short-term knob to disable the caching behavior for <64 token sessions so our demos are stable while you investigate. This is a blocker for the POC next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Zhou
Engineering Lead, BrightLane

---- end forwarded message ----

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK shim + short-term runtime workaround for BrightLane POC

Okay — with the repro we can be prescriptive. Proposed immediate plan:

Option A (fast, short-term) — SDK shim + runtime toggle (recommended)- SDK: add header switch and a tiny client-side shim to avoid chunked streaming frames for iOS network backend; SDK change can be feature-flagged and shipped as a minor patch (v0.9.9).- Runtime: add boolean config "disable_kvcache_for_short_seq" (defaults to false). When true, server will not read/write prefix cache for requests with expected sequence_length < 64. Gate: per-customer config; only available for Dedicated/Private for the first rollout.

Estimated effort: SDK patch (1-2 dev days), runtime toggle + tests (3 dev days), canary rollout + QA (1 day). Total ~5-6 dev days.

Option B (medium) — change default caching behavior (NOT recommended)

I'll spin up a short RFC and a single-test integration in our internal staging cluster. If Product approves, we can ship Option A within the BrightLane timebox.

Dev

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK shim + short-term runtime workaround for BrightLane POC

Thanks — this looks reasonable and bounded. A few product notes:

1) Approve Option A as a temporary remediation scoped to BrightLane (DEAL-9421). We want it gated per-customer and time-limited (30 days auto-expire unless extended).
2) Please create a short RFC and link to JIRA SUP-3421 for tracking. Make sure security signs off on SDK headers and any customer-scoped runtime flags (we'll need the security checklist completed before customer rollout).
3) Operationally, only allow the flag for Dedicated / Private for now. If BrightLane absolutely needs Hosted, we can evaluate a managed exception with additional auditing.

Karthik — can Product own the RFC and the canary plan? Dev/Platform, prioritize this as a hotfix. Evelyn/Marissa — I'll loop in Customer Success once the patch is scheduled so BrightLane knows the timeline.

Karthik Iyer
Group Product Manager, Redwood Inference
